title: Plane Matching Decomposition Problem
statement_text: Does there exist a constant $c>0$ such that every complete geometric graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $cn$ plane matchings?
context_text: In 2005, Araujo, Dumitrescu, Hurtado, Noy, and Urrutia asked whether the edge set of every complete geometric graph can be partitioned into a small number of crossing-free matchings. For convex position the answer is $n-1$ (or $n$), but the best known upper bound for general position is only $O(n^{3/2})$, which seems far off.
attributed_to: Araujo, Dumitrescu, Hurtado, Noy, and Urrutia
paper_contribution: Proves that for $n$ random points in $[0,1]^2$, with probability tending to 1, the edge set of $K_n[A]$ can be covered by $O(n\log n)$ crossing-free paths and $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$ crossing-free matchings, improving the general $O(n^{3/2})$ bound from [3] for this setting.
notes: The problem header uses the LaTeX auto-counter macro \thetheorem rather than an explicit number; attribution is given unambiguously in the surrounding prose referencing [3].
paper_title: Covering Complete Geometric Graphs by Monotone Paths

title: Conjecture 1.4
statement_text: For some (possibly, for every) dense $n$-element point set $A$ in general position in the plane, covering the edge set of $K_{n}[A]$ requires a superlinear number of monotone paths.
context_text: A point set in the plane is in general position if no 3 points are collinear. For a set $A$ of $n$ points in general position, the complete geometric graph $K_n[A]$ has vertex set $A$ and all $\binom{n}{2}$ straight-line segments between them as edges. A polygonal path $(v_1,\dots,v_t)$ is monotone in direction $\mathbf{u}\neq\mathbf{0}$ if $\langle \overrightarrow{v_iv_{i+1}},\mathbf{u}\rangle>0$ for every $i$, and it is monotone if it is monotone in some direction; every monotone path is crossing-free. For a constant $\alpha>0$, a set of $n$ points is $\alpha$-dense if the ratio between the longest and the shortest distance between two of its points is at most $\alpha\sqrt{n}$; 'dense' means $\alpha$-dense for some constant $\alpha$. The authors prove that for any $\alpha$-dense point set $A$ in general position, the edge set of $K_n[A]$ can be covered by $O(n^{3/2})$ monotone paths (hence decomposed into $O(n^{3/2})$ monotone matchings), and for $n$ random points in $[0,1]^2$ by $O(n\log n)$ monotone paths with high probability. They suspect the $O(n^{3/2})$ bound for dense sets is not tight but that a superlinear lower bound holds. In contrast, arbitrary point sets may require a quadratic number of monotone paths: $n^2/6+O(n)$ always suffice and some $n$-point sets require at least $n^2/15$.
paper_title: Covering Complete Geometric Graphs by Monotone Paths

title: Problem 5.1
statement_text: Does there exist a constant $c>1/2$ with the property that, for infinitely many values of $n$, there are $n$-element point sets $A$ in the plane such that every covering of the edge set of $K_{n}[A]$ by crossing-free paths requires at least $cn$ paths?
context_text: A point set in the plane is in general position if no 3 points are collinear (the paper assumes this for all point sets). For a set $A$ of $n$ points, the complete geometric graph $K_n[A]$ has vertex set $A$ and all straight-line segments between them as edges; a path (or graph) drawn this way is crossing-free (plane) if no two of its edges cross. Araujo, Dumitrescu, Hurtado, Noy and Urrutia asked whether there is a constant $c>0$ such that every complete geometric graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $cn$ plane matchings; the best known upper bound for general point sets is $O(n^{3/2})$. Obenaus and Orthaber showed that complete geometric graphs on $n$ vertices ($n$ even) cannot always be partitioned into $n/2$ plane subgraphs, but it is possible that $n/2+o(n)$ plane subgraphs always suffice. Pach, Saghafian and Schnider proved that a complete convex geometric graph on $n$ vertices cannot be decomposed into fewer than $n-1$ plane star-forests. The authors suggest that answering this problem may be a first step towards the question of Araujo et al.
paper_title: Covering Complete Geometric Graphs by Monotone Paths

title: Problem 5.2
statement_text: What is the smallest number $z=z(n)$ such that the edge set of every complete geometric graph on $n$ vertices can be covered by $z$ plane zig-zag paths?
context_text: A point set in the plane is in general position if no 3 points are collinear; a complete geometric graph on $n$ vertices is $K_n[A]$ for a set $A$ of $n$ points in general position, i.e. the points with all straight-line segments between them as edges. A path is plane if no two of its edges cross. A 3-edge path is zig-zag if its two endpoints lie in opposite open halfplanes determined by the line of its middle edge (such a path is always monotone), and a path is zig-zag if any three consecutive edges form a 3-edge zig-zag path; this does not ensure that the path is monotone or even plane. The authors show that for any finite point set $A$ in general position, the edge set of $K_n[A]$ can be covered by plane Hamiltonian zig-zag paths (every segment $ab$ lies on such a path), but the minimum number of (not necessarily Hamiltonian) plane zig-zag paths needed in the worst case is left open.
paper_title: Covering Complete Geometric Graphs by Monotone Paths
